correctness.rationale: For \(i\ne j\) the two special intermediary choices share the entry \(b_{ij}\) and jointly fail with probability \(s_p\); all other intermediates independently contribute \(q_p\). For \(i=j\), the loop contributes \(1-p\). Every joint defect event is bounded by \(s_p^{n-4}\) if source or target coincides, otherwise by \(q_p^{2n-8}\). The respective \(O(n^3)\) and \(O(n^4)\) pairs sum to \(o(n^2q_p^n)\), giving the sharp Bonferroni estimate. Diagonal and multiple-defect tails are lower order; the nonsmooth probability \(2n(1-p)^n\) is negligible because \(1-p<q_p\). Independently computed Boolean squares confirm exact finite expectations and counts for \(1\le n\le4\).

originality.rationale: The assessed claim is the explicit fixed-density leading failure equivalent, its \(10/9\) constant for uniform multipermutations, and the unique off-diagonal missing-pair law. Carvalho–Martin investigates the same monoid but different invariants; Moon–Moser established the qualitative almost-sure exponent-two property, which is credited and deliberately not claimed; Shitov recounts the distinct two-independent-factor product theorem. No matching sharp self-square rate or defect classification occurred in examined primary text and targeted published-finding searches. Absence of the 1966 full text remains an explicit material priority risk.
residual_risks: Moon–Moser (1966) original paper, whose precise quantitative estimates are unverified, could have priority for the 10/9 correction or singleton-defect limit.
Related random digraph exponent/diameter literature could give a logically equivalent sharp asymptotic without using Boolean-matrix language.
Database and web search non-hits do not prove novelty; the present originality assessment is best knowledge, not independent certification.

value.rationale: The monoid \(M_n\) of full-domain/full-range relations has a canonical absorbing universal element \(J_n\). The result quantifies first two-step absorption to a sharp exponential equivalent, identifies a unique off-diagonal exceptional relation with asymptotic conditional probability one, and explains why self-product dependence differs from two independent Boolean matrices. This is a natural asymptotic invariant and structural boundary for a complete algebra family, beyond the classical qualitative primitive exponent-two observation.
